messages:
support-jen: Hey @sean-eng, customer reported their service endpoint internal-api.acme.svc returns NXDOMAIN from inside their VPC. Public resolver returns an IP. Happening in us-west-2 only. Request ID 98765.
infra-bot: Ticket #INC-2024-312 created and escalated to netops.
sean-eng: Can you paste dig +short output from one of their app nodes?
support-jen: From app-node-01 (customer):
```
$ dig internal-api.acme.svc +short
; -> no output, returns NXDOMAIN
$ dig internal-api.acme.svc @10.0.0.2 +short
; NXDOMAIN
$ dig internal-api.acme.svc @resolver.amazonaws.com +short
54.23.12.8
```
sean-eng: Ok — public resolver returns 54.23.12.8 but their VPC resolver gives NXDOMAIN. Any recent private hosted zone (PHZ) changes?
lucy-netops: I see a PHZ named acme.svc created in acct A yesterday. Looks like it was associated to their app VPC (vpc-0aa1). That would shadow the AWS-managed service endpoint records.
matt-sre: Also noticed a Route53 resolver rule created in acct B forwarding *.acme.svc to 10.2.2.2 earlier this week. Not sure if that's associated to their VPC though.
support-jen: Customer confirms they created a PHZ acme.svc to manage some internal records. They didn't intend to override the service endpoints. They also have a forwarder rule in a different account.
sean-eng: PHZ on the VPC is the likely cause — split-horizon: the PHZ takes precedence so queries won't fall through to the AWS-managed zone. Two quick checks: (1) which account owns the PHZ, (2) which VPCs are associated. Run: 
```
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name acme.svc
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id <PHZ-ID>
```
 (replace with their PHZ id).
support-jen: Ran list-hosted-zones-by-name for them. PHZ id ZPHZ-ACME owned by acct A. Associated VPCs: vpc-0aa1 (app), vpc-0bb2 (dev). The resolver forwarder exists in acct B but is NOT associated to their app VPC (so it's irrelevant here).
lucy-netops: Confirmed — if PHZ is associated, it wins. Since it has no record for internal-api.acme.svc, you get NXDOMAIN. The root cause is accidental PHZ shadowing. Fix options: disassociate the PHZ from the app VPC or delete the PHZ. If they need a PHZ for other internal names, create a subzone (e.g., internal.acme.svc) instead.
matt-sre: FYI when I tried hitting the service IP from our probe I saw intermittent TLS errors / 403s: looks like SNI mismatch on some paths (hostname internal-api.acme.svc vs cert CN service.internal.aws). Might be due to some requests routing to a public-backed endpoint IP.
support-jen: Repro steps sent to customer:
- from app node: dig internal-api.acme.svc -> NXDOMAIN
- from public resolver: dig -> 54.23.12.8
- curl https://internal-api.acme.svc -v -> SSL alert / sometimes 403 (intermittent)
They asked for a quick config change that won't break service endpoints.
sean-eng: Short-term remediation: disassociate PHZ acme.svc from the app VPC (fast). Long-term: avoid creating a PHZ that matches the service endpoint domain. If they need internal records, use a deeper subdomain. I'll draft an advisory KB.
support-jen: Customer disassociated the PHZ at 2024-04-12T14:21:03Z. After disassociation: 
```
$ dig internal-api.acme.svc +short
54.23.12.8
$ curl -v https://internal-api.acme.svc 2>&1 | sed -n '1,8p'
* Connected to 54.23.12.8 (54.23.12.8) port 443
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
Customer confirms endpoints are healthy again. :party_parrot:
eng-oncall: Note: warn customer about brief client reconnections during disassociation. Monitor for 15m and send logs if problems persist.
support-jen: Customer monitored 20m, no regressions. They were advised to remove the PHZ or move to subzone. I also provided step-by-step AWS CLI commands and the KB link.
sean-eng: Please file a short postmortem (root cause: accidental PHZ creation shadowing AWS-managed service endpoint). Recommend adding a KB specific to service endpoints + split-horizon traps.
support-jen: Filed KB draft: /docs/support/kb/private-dns-service-endpoint-shadowing.md
matt-sre: Incident resolved and closed. :white_check_mark:
